title: What is yours
lesson: You did not control the relationship. You control your actions. Nothing else was ever yours to lose.
action: Write three things you control today. Ignore the rest.

title: Their choice, not your verdict
lesson: A person left. That is a fact about the person. It says nothing about your worth, unless you decide it does.
action: Write the story you are telling about what this means about you. Then delete it.

title: Expect the hard moment
lesson: You will want to message them. Know this now. What is expected hurts less than what surprises you.
action: Write down your hardest moment today. Decide now what you will do instead of messaging.

title: See it from far away
lesson: Picture your whole life. This relationship is a small part of it. It only feels huge because you are close to it.
action: Write two sentences about this moment, from five years in the future.

title: Stop checking
lesson: You cannot control what they think or do. Checking for signs gives you no answers. It only keeps you attached.
action: Each time you want to check on them today, write it down instead of checking.

title: Use what happened
lesson: This is not good or bad. It is simply what happened. You can only build your next step from what is real.
action: Finish this sentence: Because this happened, I can now ___.

title: One week is real progress
lesson: Seven days without contact is not luck. It is proof you can do this.
action: Write one sentence about what helped you get through the hardest day this week.

title: Comparison is not information
lesson: You do not know their life right now. Comparing your grief to their apparent ease tells you nothing true. It only adds weight you chose to carry.
action: Write one sentence about what you actually know, not what you imagine.

title: Build the smallest routine
lesson: A body in chaos needs order it can trust. Not motivation. Repetition.
action: Pick one thing to do at the same time every day this week. Nothing more.

title: Ten days
lesson: Ten days of choosing this path is not small. It is the foundation the next twenty stand on.
action: Write one sentence naming what ten days has already proven about you.

title: Stop rewriting the past
lesson: You keep imagining a better version of what happened. That version does not exist. Only the real one can teach you anything.
action: Write one true thing this relationship taught you.

title: Feel it, then stop
lesson: Grief that passes through you is normal. Grief that you keep calling back is a habit, not a feeling.
action: Set a timer for ten minutes. Feel what you feel. When it ends, do something else.

title: Picture the hardest scene
lesson: Imagine seeing them with someone new. You have survived harder things already. Picture it now, calmly, so it loses its power over you.
action: Write two sentences describing yourself in that moment, calm.

title: Their new life is not yours to audit
lesson: What they do now, who they see, how quickly they move on — none of it is evidence about you. It is simply what they are doing.
action: Each time you catch yourself checking, write it down instead.

title: It was real, not a mistake
lesson: Calling the whole relationship a mistake erases what was true in it. It happened, it mattered, and it ended. All three are facts.
action: Write one sentence that is true about the relationship, without judging it good or bad.

title: A good memory will surface
lesson: A good memory will come today, uninvited. It is not a sign to return. It is simply a memory.
action: When it comes, name it as a memory, not a message. Then continue your day.

title: You are past the hardest math
lesson: The distance between the version of you two weeks ago and the version of you now is larger than it feels day to day.
action: Write one thing that used to take everything you had, and now takes less.

title: You do not control the schedule
lesson: Grief has its own pace. Rushing it does not speed it up. It only adds a second frustration on top of the first.
action: Write one sentence letting go of a timeline you set for yourself.

title: What this reveals about your needs
lesson: Every relationship reveals what you actually need, usually by its absence. This one is still teaching you that, even now.
action: Name one need that went unmet. Not to blame — to know it.

title: Twenty days
lesson: You are two-thirds through this structure, not because the calendar demands it, but because you kept choosing it.
action: Write one sentence about what changed in how you handle a hard moment, compared to day one.

title: You are not who you were
lesson: Day-one you could not have done what today-you just did. That's not a metaphor. That's rebuilt.
action: Name one thing you handled this week that would have wrecked you three weeks ago.

title: Set the floor
lesson: You don't choose who you meet next. You choose the standard you stop negotiating. Set it now.
action: Write one non-negotiable you're carrying forward.

title: Boredom is not a relapse
lesson: Some days will simply be flat. That is not the relationship's absence catching up with you. That is an ordinary day.
action: Do one thing today for no reason other than that you wanted to.

title: Other people's opinions of your pace
lesson: Someone may think you moved on too fast, or too slow. Their timeline for you is not yours to manage.
action: Write one sentence about your own pace, without defending it to anyone.

title: Prepare to see them with someone new, for real
lesson: At some point this will happen, not in imagination but in fact. Deciding now how you will carry yourself removes the ambush later.
action: Write two sentences: what you will do in the first minute if this happens.

title: What you would tell someone else
lesson: If a friend described your exact situation to you, you would have clear advice. Distance makes things obvious. Borrow that clarity for yourself.
action: Write the advice you would give a friend in your exact position.

title: Readiness is not a feeling you wait for
lesson: You will not wake up one day simply feeling ready to date again. Readiness is closer to a decision than a sensation.
action: Write one sentence about what you are actually ready for right now, separate from what you feel.

title: The standard you now hold
lesson: You cannot make the last relationship different. You can make the next one start from what you now know.
action: Write one standard, in one sentence, that you did not have before this happened.

title: Twenty-nine days of evidence
lesson: This is not a mood that happened to hold. It is a record of choices, made on purpose, most days in a row.
action: Write one sentence naming what you are proud of, without qualifying it.

title: The program ends. The practice does not.
lesson: Thirty days does not mean the grief is finished. It means you now have a way to meet it that does not require this structure to keep working.
action: Write one sentence about what you will keep doing, starting tomorrow, without the app telling you to.
